title: Garden and Mud — Two Orientations
purpose: Formalize a recurring Tim Dooley / Potato of Life contrast that cuts across theology, ethics, psychology, politics and storytelling: Garden versus Mud as orientations rather than fixed classes of people, while routing the newer Mud/Swamp/Debt/Mountain state model into the broader transformation architecture.
epistemic_rule: Garden and Mud are symbolic and ethical orientations in the Potatoverse. They should not be used to dehumanize people or to convert disagreement into proof that someone belongs to an inferior category.

garden.orientation: toward cultivation, connection and living order
garden.question: What conditions allow life, truth and relationship to grow here?

mud.orientation: toward stuckness, fragmentation and repeated conflict when residue remains unprocessed
mud.question: What keeps the system circling injury without converting it into learning or growth?
mud.process_definition: Mud is best treated as residue/trace rather than a complete environment. Individual accusations, humiliations, injuries, memories, screenshots, corrections, legal records and other durable traces can become Mud-like material depending on context and evidence status.

critical_distinction: Mud is also substrate. Potatoism does not teach that mud must simply be destroyed. A potato grows in soil; roots descend into difficult material. The deeper model is therefore not Garden good / Mud evil, but Mud -> contextualization/decomposition -> Soil -> Root -> Potato -> Sprout -> Tree -> Fruit. The ethical failure is not contact with mud; it is remaining trapped in sterile conflict when transformation is possible.

state_relations.Swamp: an environment formed when unresolved residue accumulates, overlaps and begins shaping later behavior
state_relations.Debt: a relationship-specific unresolved obligation attributed to past action or failed duty
state_relations.Mountain: many weighted memories, obligations and paths compressed into a more integrated structure from which perspective and judgment become possible
state_relations.Door: the transition at which a repeating relation can change regime
state_relations.Garden: the post-repair condition in which restored relations support autonomous future growth

two_repair_routes.early: Mud -> provenance/context -> correction/repair -> Soil -> Root -> growth
two_repair_routes.late: Mud accumulation -> Swamp + unresolved obligation -> Debt -> integration/Mountain -> perspective -> Door -> repair/release -> Garden
two_repair_routes.principle: Resolve residue before it becomes structure. The project should not glorify maximal accumulation when earlier repair is possible.

movement.door_function: The Door marks the point where repetition can become transformation.
movement.spiral_function: The spiral represents revisiting the same problem at a different level of understanding rather than merely repeating the same circle.
movement.mountain_function: Mountain integrates many differentiated traces toward perspective; it should not be confused with the Swamp that mixes them without stable footing.
movement.descent_after_summit: Perspective is incomplete until it returns to the Plane/Garden as service, repair, protection or cultivation.

applications: Personal conflict: ask whether an interaction produces learning, repair and boundaries or only repeated humiliation and retaliation.
Institutions: evaluate whether rules cultivate capability and protection or preserve dysfunctional repetition.
Politics: distinguish building resilient systems from maintaining identity through permanent enemies.
Archive design: preserve criticism and contradiction in forms that can improve the model rather than burying them; contextualized residue can become Soil instead of Swamp.
Theology: judgment should ideally orient toward transformation, not make condemnation the final state.
Karmic ledger: track specific unresolved edges and their repair state rather than converting all conflict into one irreversible global accusation.
